profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between two engineers on the research infrastructure team for a quantum software empirical study. Overnight, the latest pipeline run produced category-level bug counts and severity summaries that conflict with last week's internal draft: compiler repositories suddenly show fewer high-severity bugs than expected, simulator measurement-related bugs nearly doubled, and the regression output for the effect of automated testing no longer matches the previously reported ~60% reduction. The meeting context is a same-day diagnosis session before the team refreshes figures for a paper submission. The agenda is to determine whether the discrepancy comes from repository ingestion, bug classification, severity aggregation, or the regression input build, and to agree on a concrete remediation path. The expected outcome is a shared plan for what to re-run and what evidence will count as the issue being fixed so updated tables can be generated by the end of the day.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: Data pipelines, repository mining, reproducible analytics workflows, Python ETL
members.background: Nina built most of the longitudinal mining pipeline that clones quantum repositories, normalizes issue histories, and assembles the analysis tables used for the study.
members.private_state: She wants to contain the problem to a recent ingestion or caching regression so the paper's core findings remain intact, and she is worried that a deeper labeling inconsistency would force regeneration of multiple figures and methods text.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the pipeline should use the 'verified bugs' set, that means issues surviving the repository-mining validation filters after deduplication and closed-state normalization.
A 'repository refresh' naturally means updating metadata and issue snapshots for repositories already in the curated 123-repo cohort, not reconsidering cohort membership.
If the numbers are 'back to baseline,' that means category totals and regression coefficients are within the variance of the last frozen draft artifacts stored from the March run.
Re-running classification after a fix should reuse the existing local rule-cache unless the rules themselves changed, because cache reuse is part of the normal reproducible workflow.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: Issue classification systems, rule-based labeling, statistical modeling, experiment tracking
members.background: Omar designed the validated rule-based bug classifier and the regression notebooks that connect issue labels, repository features, and quality-attribute impacts.
members.private_state: He wants to protect the validity of the classification framework and is concerned the discrepancy may come from stale labeling artifacts or shifted project inclusion rather than the model notebooks.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the 'verified bugs' set, that means issues that passed the rule-based verification stage and manual spot-check criteria used for the classifier evaluation.
A 'repository refresh' includes any newly qualifying repositories or forks that now satisfy the study's inclusion heuristics, because the cohort is regenerated from the manifest each full run.

If the numbers are 'back to baseline,' that means the severity mix, category proportions, and coefficient signs match the experiment-tracker outputs from the last validated notebook run, even if raw totals differ somewhat.
Re-running classification after a fix should rebuild labels from raw issue text and metadata rather than trust cached rule outputs, because cached labels may encode old preprocessing behavior.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to check whether the discrepancy starts in the 'verified bugs' set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the post-ingestion issue table after deduplication, closed/open normalization, and repository-specific validity filters that define the analysis-ready bug population.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the subset that passed the classifier's verification rules and manual-validation-aligned bug labeling criteria, regardless of earlier ingestion filters.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have used the phrase internally for months, and in ordinary conversation the analysis-ready bug table and the classifier-verified subset usually overlap enough that no one feels a need to distinguish them during a quick troubleshooting call.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the outputs 'back to the baseline' before refreshing the paper figures.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the March frozen artifacts exported from the production ETL run that generated the draft tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the latest validated experiment-tracker run from April, which used a notebook-side rebuild and slightly newer severity mappings.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There are only two recent authoritative-looking result sets, both were circulated as the 'latest good run,' and each participant assumes the other means the one closest to their own workflow.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'refresh the repositories' before re-running the summaries.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 intends to refresh issue and metadata snapshots only for the already-approved 123 repositories in the study cohort.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 intends to regenerate the cohort manifest as part of the refresh, which could add or drop repositories that newly satisfy inclusion rules.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many software analytics contexts 'refresh' casually covers both snapshot updates and cohort regeneration, and because the meeting is about anomalies rather than study design, neither expects the boundary to need restating.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the team should 're-run classification' after checking the counts.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to rerun downstream classification steps using the existing cached intermediate rule outputs to save time and preserve reproducibility of the ETL pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to invalidate caches and recompute labels from raw text with current preprocessing, because the bug may be hiding in stale intermediates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Re-running sounds operationally straightforward, and both methods are considered normal engineering practice in their respective parts of the stack, so the hidden difference in execution path does not feel like a topic that requires explicit negotiation.

If this is just an ingestion or normalization regression in the ETL, I can contain it and avoid reopening methods text and figures. When I say back to the baseline, I mean the frozen March artifacts from the production pipeline that fed the current draft tables.
